text: BLNK. Creative Studio (بلنك ستوديو الإبداعي) is a creative studio founded in 2014, headquartered in Beirut, Lebanon. BLNK. is a Beirut-based creative studio founded in 2014. We specialize in brand identity, digital design, and visual systems for companies across the Gulf region that want to grow with intention and clarity. The studio has 10+ years active and has built 50+ brands. BLNK. serves clients across the GCC market, focusing on Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman.
BLNK. Creative Studio was founded by Dena Rifai, who serves as Founder & Creative Director. The studio's office is located at Pierre Gemayel Avenue, Rive Gauche Tower, 20th Floor, Beirut.

BLNK.'s project process, step 1 - Discover (الاستكشاف): includes Brand audit & analysis; Competitor research; Stakeholder interviews; Market positioning.
BLNK.'s project process, step 2 - Define (التحديد): includes Brand strategy; Messaging framework; Creative brief; Visual direction.
BLNK.'s project process, step 3 - Design (التصميم): includes Logo concepts; Visual identity system; Design & feedback rounds; Final refinements.
BLNK.'s project process, step 4 - Deliver (التسليم): includes Final files in all formats; Brand book handover; Implementation support; Post-launch guidance.

BLNK.'s overall workflow moves through four phases in order: Discover, Define, Design, Deliver — from initial brand audit and research through strategy, design execution, and final delivery with post-launch support.

BLNK. does not quote fixed prices upfront. Pricing depends on a discovery conversation and is determined by several factors specific to each project rather than a flat rate.

Factors that influence BLNK.'s pricing for a branding project: scope of deliverables (e.g. logo only vs. full brand identity system with brand book), number of stationery items needed (business cards, letterhead, envelopes, signage), whether packaging design is required, and whether the client needs both Arabic and English versions of all assets.

Factors that influence BLNK.'s pricing for digital/website projects: number of pages, complexity of features (e.g. e-commerce, booking systems, custom integrations), whether it's a new build or a redesign, and the required timeline (rush projects may cost more).

Factors that influence BLNK.'s pricing for social media management: number of platforms covered, posting frequency (content calendar volume), whether content creation (photography/video) is included or only design/templates, and whether community management/replies are part of the scope.

BLNK.'s general approach to pricing conversations: the studio avoids quoting a fixed number before understanding the project. Instead, pricing is discussed after a short discovery meeting where the client's industry, company size, project scope, and goals are understood, followed by a tailored written proposal reflecting those specifics.

BLNK.'s general approach with budget-sensitive clients: when a lead raises cost concerns or has a limited budget, the recommended response is to acknowledge the concern without quoting a number immediately, and to explain that pricing depends on company size, project scope, and required services — with a discovery conversation used to tailor the best-fit package and price for that client's situation.

Customer objection pattern: 'Do you have experience with luxury branding in the GCC?' This is a credibility/trust check, typically asked immediately by ad-sourced leads before any pricing or scope discussion. Recommended response: lead with confidence and immediately share proof — the company profile/portfolio PDF — before asking clarifying questions.

Customer objection pattern: 'Can I know who is the owner of the agency?' A prospect may ask for ownership or leadership details as a legitimacy check before committing to a discovery call. Recommended response: answer promptly with the founder's name (Dena Rifai, Founder & Creative Director) and move directly to booking the discovery call rather than over-explaining.

Customer objection pattern: 'Please share your website and portfolio of work done' before agreeing to any meeting. Recommended response: respond promptly with the studio website (www.bliynk.com) and company profile PDF. Note: if a specific meeting time is proposed too soon after this exchange, before rapport is built, the lead may stall or go quiet on scheduling — better to confirm interest and general timeline first before pushing a specific slot.

Customer objection pattern: budget caution from a small or pre-launch business — e.g. 'we are a small shop, limited capital, very cautious about spend, can you share pricing or packages upfront so we know if it fits our budget.' This is a proactive cost objection raised before any proposal has been made. Recommended response: acknowledge the concern directly, avoid quoting numbers immediately, and redirect toward a short discovery call framed as the way to get the best-fit price.

General objection-handling principle observed across BLNK. leads: nearly every inbound lead opens with some form of credibility check (portfolio proof, ownership, regional/industry experience) before discussing scope or budget. The consistent, effective response pattern is to answer the trust question promptly and concretely (name, portfolio, or relevant case study), then move quickly toward booking a short discovery call rather than continuing an extended text exchange.

BLNK.'s general policy on meeting reschedules: when a client needs to postpone a scheduled discovery call, the studio accommodates the new time without pushback, confirms the rescheduled slot clearly, and sends a fresh meeting link ahead of time.

FAQ: What happens after the discovery call? Following a discovery meeting, BLNK.'s team prepares a tailored written proposal based on the client's stated industry, company size, goals, and requirements. Turnaround time varies by project complexity, but proposals are generally sent within a few business days of the discovery call.

FAQ: How long does a discovery call take? BLNK.'s discovery meetings are kept short — typically 10 to 20 minutes on Zoom — and usually include the Business Development Manager and the Creative Director, to understand the client's needs and explain BLNK.'s services before proposing next steps.

FAQ: What is BLNK.'s project workflow? Projects move through four phases: Discover (brand audit, competitor research, stakeholder interviews, market positioning), Define (brand strategy, messaging framework, creative brief, visual direction), Design (logo concepts, visual identity system, feedback rounds, final refinements), and Deliver (final files in all formats, brand book handover, implementation support, post-launch guidance).

FAQ: Does BLNK. work in both Arabic and English? Yes. BLNK. offers full bilingual creative capability from brand strategy through final files, with no translation gaps — meaning design and messaging are developed natively in both languages rather than translated after the fact.

FAQ: What industries does BLNK. have experience in? BLNK. has worked across real estate, food & beverage, finance & corporate, industrial & services, tech & entertainment, and beauty & wellness sectors, with clients spanning Lebanon, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, and beyond.

FAQ: How does BLNK. communicate with clients during a project? BLNK. offers direct access to the creative team — there are no account managers or intermediaries. Clients work directly with the creative leads assigned to their project.

General pricing principle at BLNK.: cost is not fixed and depends on multiple variables including company size, industry, the specific service(s) requested (branding, digital, print, or social media), project complexity, number of deliverables, and timeline urgency. There is no single price list — every quote is tailored after understanding these factors.
